item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports textual item representations for sparse recommendation, but the retrieved evidence does not directly establish gains for a GRU trained from scratch on titles/descriptions. [Recformer (KDD 2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) reports improvements in low-resource and cold-start settings using textual item attributes, but uses a Transformer with pretraining and finetuning. [DWSRec (AAAI 2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) shows that the geometry of pretrained text embeddings affects sequential recommendation quality; its results cannot establish the effectiveness of randomly initialized text encoders. [Content-Based Initialization (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19473) reports benefits from adding small trainable residuals to frozen content embeddings, highlighting a tradeoff between recommendation adaptation and preservation of semantic structure.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis: retain one GRU recommender per category; represent each item with its ID embedding plus a jointly trained, compact title/description encoder using randomly initialized token embeddings, masked mean pooling and projection. Share this representation between history inputs and candidate scoring so recommendation gradients train the text pathway directly. Shared tokens could transfer learning from frequent items to sparse items and distinguish specific product terms; these are plausible mechanisms, not demonstrated gains under the requested constraints. Compare against the corrected ID-only GRU using the fixed macro validation HR@10; inspect sparse-item performance separately to determine whether content helps. Use only available titles/descriptions, with no external weights, extra metadata or separately fitted scoring model."}
